members.title: Access to {{space}}
members.resetOnly: You do not see this client. As the operator you can change rights but not give yourself one.

inviteLink.title: Invite
inviteLink.text: A link to pass on. Whoever follows it makes an account, or joins with the one they have.

members.lastManagerRole: You are the only one who may manage this client. Give that up and only the operator can manage it, and you can no longer invite anyone.
members.lastManagerLeave: You are the only one who may manage this client. Leave and only the operator can manage it.
members.invitedName: If there is an account “{{name}}”, it finds the invitation under “New” and accepts or declines it.

sidebar.label: Clients
sidebar.noFavorites: Star a client to keep it here.

share.title: Share “{{title}}”
share.whoHint: Everyone with access to {{space}}, with their right there.
share.publicHint: Anyone with the link can look, nobody can change anything. Only if the operator allows public pages.
share.onlyManagers: Only those who manage the client switch the public page.
share.operatorOff: The operator has not allowed public pages (Settings, Server).

settings.title: Settings

start.title: Start page
start.text: What shows first after signing in.

language.title: Language
language.text: nexbrand brings English and German. Upload more under Server, Languages; whatever a file lacks shows in English.
language.textMember: nexbrand brings English and German; the operator can add more languages.
language.templateHint: The English texts as a file to translate. Upload it under Server, Languages with a code such as es or pt-BR.

looks.title: Light or dark
looks.text: In this browser, like the switch top right.

settings.accessHint: Access is given per client: to people and to teams, to read, write or manage. Whoever makes a client manages it.

server.oidcHint: For example authentik, set up as in nexlore and nextrmnl.
server.publicHint: Off out of the box. When on, those who manage a client may share a version as a read-only page and put drafts to the client for review.
server.backupsHint: Clients, versions, files and the database in one archive. Restoring shows a dry run first.
server.languagesHint: German and English are built in. Add more as a JSON file; missing texts fall back to English.
server.logHint: Four levels as in every nex app. The two deep ones switch themselves off after an hour. Never client contents, passwords or keys.
server.stripLocation: Take place and device out of photos
server.stripLocationHint: Phones write where a photo was taken and with what. On by default.
server.mailHint: Only for invitations. Without a server, the link to copy is enough.
server.secretKept: Kept; type only to change it.
server.passwordLoginHint: Off: members get in through the provider only. You as the operator can always use your password.
server.twoFactorRequiredHint: Every account that signs in with a password must set one up before it gets further. Accounts from the provider bring its own. Switch on your own first.
server.oidcAutoCreateHint: Off: only invited or linked accounts get in.
server.publicUrlHint: For links in invitations and public pages, and the OIDC return.
server.passwordGiven: The new password, to pass on once:

role.title: Change the role of {{name}}?
role.text: Operators change every setting of this server.

delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
delete.text: The account goes; its clients stay, with everyone else who has access.

password.title: New password for {{name}}?
password.text: A random one is made; every sign-in of the account ends.

reset.title: Take the second factor of {{name}}?
reset.text: For a lost phone: the account signs in with its password only, until it sets up a new one.

signout.title: Sign {{name}} out everywhere?
signout.text: Every browser of the account has to sign in again.

backup_restore.title: Restore this backup?
backup_restore.text: The present state is kept as a backup first. nexbrand restarts, everybody signs in again.

backup_download.title: Download this backup?
backup_download.text: It holds every client, file and account. It is not encrypted.

unblock.title: Unblock {{name}}?
unblock.text: {{name}} can sign in again afterwards, with their own password or through the sign-in provider.

server.checkOk: Whole: {{clients}} clients, {{files}} files. A restore would add {{add}} files and remove {{remove}}.
server.checkBad: Damaged: this backup cannot be restored.
server.restarting: nexbrand restarts with the backup. The page reloads in a moment.
server.languageAdded: Language added. It shows in the account menu after reloading.
server.logClearText: Every line goes. New ones come as before.

allSpaces.title: Every client and its access
allSpaces.text: Every client with its managers. As the operator you see and manage every client. If you change rights on a client you are not part of yourself, those involved hear of it.
allSpaces.membersCreateHint: Off: only the operator makes clients and gives others access. Whoever makes a client manages it.

authentik.title: authentik in one step
authentik.text: With an API token that may create applications, nexbrand sets up provider and application in authentik itself. The token is used for that only and never stored.

server.publicAllowedHint: Those who manage a client may then make read-only pages and reviews. Switched off, every link answers as if it had never existed.
server.filesHint: Logos, fonts and example files: how large they may be and what is taken out when uploading.
server.inviteText: Without a client: the new account makes clients of its own or gets access to others later.

apiTokens.title: API tokens
apiTokens.text: Accounts connect nexbrand with programs such as nexdeck or n8n. A token only reads, and never more than its account. Off by default.
apiTokens.allowHint: Every account makes its own tokens under My account → Connections.
apiTokens.blockText: The token then answers like none, for good. The account sees it as “blocked by the operator” and may make a new one while API tokens are on.
apiTokens.offHint: Switch API tokens off and every token answers 401. The tokens stay and work again when you switch them on.

server.ownSecondFactorFirst: Set up your own second factor first (My account, Security), or you would be the first one who cannot go on.

outside.title: Collecting and AI
outside.text: Two ways out, both closed until you open them. When collecting, the website learns that this server asked for it; with AI, a client's material goes to the service an account has entered.
outside.collect: Allow collecting from websites and GitHub repositories
outside.collectHint: Addresses in the own network are always blocked. A client's PDFs work without this switch; they never leave the house.
outside.githubHint: Leave empty for public repositories. A token that may read contents is enough; it is stored encrypted and never shown again.
outside.ai: Allow each account its own AI service
outside.aiHint: Each account enters its service and key itself. The AI sorts what was collected and proposes directions in the wizard; nexbrand always measures the values.
outside.hosts: Machines in the own network an AI service may run on
outside.hostsHint: One name or address per line, with a port if you like, for Ollama at home for example. Everything else in the own network stays blocked.

errors.locale_unusable: This language file cannot be used.
errors.path_too_long: The name or path is too long.
errors.name_invalid: This name cannot be used: it holds a character or a form Windows, macOS or Linux cannot store.
errors.name_invalid_dot: A name may not begin with a dot: such files are hidden on many systems.
errors.name_invalid_control: The name holds an invisible control character.
errors.name_invalid_char: The character {{char}} cannot stand in a name: Windows, macOS or Linux cannot store it, or links use it.
errors.name_invalid_edge: A name may not begin with a space nor end with a space or a dot.
errors.name_invalid_reserved: “{{word}}” is a reserved name on Windows.
errors.exists: Something of that name exists already.
errors.locked: Somebody else is editing this note.
errors.not_a_note: This file is not a note.
errors.too_large_for_trash: The file is too large for the trash.
errors.archive_invalid: This is not a ZIP archive.
errors.archive_unsafe: The archive holds an entry that would end up outside its folder. Nothing was unpacked.
errors.archive_too_many_files: The archive holds too many files.
errors.client_required: The request did not say which tab sent it. Reload the page.
errors.changed_meanwhile: The note was changed again in the meantime. Nothing was overwritten; open the comparison again.
errors.quota_exceeded: There is no space left for your files. Delete some you do not need, or ask the operator for more.
errors.network_error: The server could not be reached.
errors.account_locked: Too many wrong passwords. The account waits a quarter of an hour.
errors.too_many_attempts: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.password_login_off: Signing in with a password is turned off.
errors.unknown_language: nexbrand does not have this language.
errors.invite_invalid: This invitation is not valid any more.
errors.operator_only: Only the operator may do this.
errors.last_manager: The client needs another manager first.
errors.no_such_account: There is no account of that name.
errors.not_a_member: This account has no access to the client.
errors.invalid_days: Choose one of the offered durations.
errors.invalid_email: This is not a mail address.
errors.mail_off: No mail server is set up.
errors.mail_failed: The mail server did not take the mail.
errors.cannot_delete_self: You cannot delete your own account.
errors.cannot_demote_self: You cannot take the operator role from yourself.
errors.oidc_account: This account signs in through the provider.
errors.oidc_only_account: This account signs in through the provider only.
errors.oidc_not_configured: No sign-in provider is set up.
errors.oidc_no_account: There is no account for you here. Ask for an invitation.
errors.oidc_email_unverified: The provider did not confirm your mail address.
errors.oidc_email_taken: Your mail address belongs to another account.
errors.oidc_state_mismatch: The sign-in ran out or came from elsewhere. Try again.
errors.oidc_token_invalid: The provider's answer was not valid.
errors.oidc_denied: The provider did not let you in.
errors.oidc_link_mismatch: This link belongs to another account.
errors.oidc_subject_taken: This identity is linked to another account already.
errors.issuer_invalid: This is not an OpenID Connect provider.
errors.issuer_unreachable: The provider cannot be reached at this address.
errors.url_invalid: The address must start with http:// or https://.
errors.backup_invalid: This is not a nexbrand backup.
errors.backup_damaged: The backup is damaged. Nothing was changed.
errors.busy: nexbrand is busy. Try again in a moment.
errors.scan_running: The vault is being read already.
errors.task_changed: This task changed in its note meanwhile.
errors.totp_enabled: The second factor is on already.
errors.totp_not_enabled: The second factor is not on.
errors.totp_enrolment_expired: The setup took too long. Start again.
errors.totp_code_wrong: The code is not right. Check the time on your phone and try the next one.
errors.second_factor_expired: Too many wrong codes, or too long a wait. Start again with your password.
errors.second_factor_unavailable: The second factor cannot be checked on this installation. Ask the operator to reset it.
errors.second_factor_setup_required: Set up your second factor first.
errors.own_second_factor_first: Set up your own second factor first, on your account page.
errors.use_disable: Turn your own second factor off on your account page.
errors.share_password_short: The password needs at least {{min}} characters.
errors.provider_first: Set up a sign-in provider first, or nobody but you could sign in.
errors.bad_view: The view cannot be read. Check the YAML: indentation, colons and quotes.
errors.bad_day_format: This pattern cannot name every day: year, month and day as numbers; names of months or weekdays do not work.
errors.oauth_client: This program is not registered here. Start the sign-in again from the program.
errors.oauth_redirect: This program did not register the address it wants to go back to.
errors.oauth_pkce: This program does not sign in safely (PKCE with S256 is missing).
errors.oauth_response_type: This program asks for something nexbrand does not give.
errors.request_closed: This request was decided already or ran out.
errors.request_changed: This request does not match what was asked; nothing ran.
errors.notify_no_way: Give a webhook address or switch mail on first.
errors.api_off: The operator has not switched API tokens on.
errors.too_many_tokens: An account holds at most 20 tokens.
errors.operator_network: The operator's settings are open only from the home network.
errors.display_name_taken: Another account goes by this name.
errors.display_name_invalid: A display name cannot hold control or invisible characters.
errors.public_url_missing: Mail needs the public address of nexbrand; the operator sets it under Settings.
errors.internal_error: Something went wrong on the server.
errors.too_large: The file is larger than allowed ({{max_mb}} MB).
errors.upload_aborted: The upload stopped before the end.
errors.shares_off: The operator has not allowed public pages.
errors.invalid_title: Please give a name of 1 to 200 characters.
errors.not_found: Not found, or not open to you.
errors.forbidden: Your right on this client does not allow this.
errors.setup_code_wrong: The setup code is wrong. It stands in the server log.
errors.invalid_canvas: This is not a JSON Canvas file (.canvas) or an archive with one (.zip).
errors.empty_canvas: There is nothing on this canvas to bring in.
errors.packages_empty_svg: The SVG file holds nothing that can be drawn.
errors.template_not_json: This is no nexbrand template file.
errors.lead_not_member: The lead must be in the team.
errors.team_not_local: The members of this team are kept elsewhere.
errors.managed_by_suite: This is kept in nexsuite now.
errors.suite_refused: nexsuite does not know this app any more.

errors.emergency_code_wrong: This emergency code is not valid.
errors.disconnect_in_suite: Disconnect in nexsuite under Apps, or with the emergency account of this app.
errors.person_twice: Each person in nexsuite can be matched once only.
errors.space_twice: Each client in nexsuite can be chosen once only.
errors.team_twice: Each team in nexsuite can be matched once only.
errors.connecting_already: A connection is under way already: resume it or give it up.
errors.invalid_set: A value of this CI is not right.
errors.published: A published version never changes. Make a new version.
errors.in_use: A project builds on this draft. Move the project first.
errors.too_many_versions: This client has as many versions as it may hold.
errors.too_many_projects: This client has as many projects as it may hold.
errors.not_published: Only a published version can be shared.
errors.review_open: This draft is before the client already.
errors.not_a_draft: Only a draft goes before the client.
errors.too_many_shares: This client has as many public pages as it may.
errors.too_many_comments: This review holds as many comments as it may.
errors.no_version: There is no published version for that day.
errors.not_a_picture: This is not a picture that works as a logo.

errors.collect_off: The operator has not allowed collecting from websites and repositories.

errors.ai_hosts_invalid: One of the machines is not a valid name.
errors.ai_no_list: The service names no models. Enter the model by hand.
errors.ai_not_json: The AI did not answer in the format asked for.
errors.ai_unreadable: The AI's answer could not be read.
errors.ai_service_busy: The service is busy right now. Try again in a moment.
errors.ai_text_too_long: Too much material at once (at most {{max}} characters).
errors.ai_timeout: The service did not answer within {{seconds}} seconds.
errors.ai_too_often: Too many requests in one minute.
errors.ai_unreachable: The server cannot reach the service.
errors.client_twice: Each client in nexsuite can be chosen once only.
errors.collect_name_first: Enter the name of the new client first.

setup.title: Set up nexbrand
setup.text: The first account runs this server: it may invite others and change every setting.
setup.codeHint: It stands in the server log (docker logs nexbrand), or set NEXBRAND_SETUP_TOKEN.

login.title: Sign in
login.passwordOff: Sign-in with a password is turned off for members.

code.title: Second factor
code.text: The code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code.
code.label: Code
code.hint: Six digits, or a recovery code from paper.

invite.title: Invitation
invite.intoSpace: You get access to the client “{{space}}” ({{role}}).
invite.invalidText: This invitation was used or has run out. Ask for a new one.
invite.noWay: Sign-in with a password is off and no sign-in provider is set up. Ask the operator.

public.gone: This page does not exist any more, or its link ran out.
public.title: {{name}}: brand guidelines
public.reviewGone: This review does not exist any more. Please ask the agency for a new link.

about.subtitle: Every client's corporate design in one place: colours, fonts, logos, in versions.

updates.title: Updates
updates.text: Whether a newer version of nexbrand is out.
updates.dailyHint: Asks GitHub for the newest release. Off: only when you press the button.
updates.whatGoesOut: Only the question goes out: a request to api.github.com for the newest release of nexbrand, with no names, clients or settings. It is the only call nexbrand makes on its own.

notices.operator_role: The operator {{actor}} changed the right of {{subject}} in “{{space}}” ({{role}})

me.title: My account

profile.displayHint: How others see you. Empty shows your user name {{name}}; you still sign in with it.
profile.name: Name
profile.hint: A photo from your phone or camera. It is cut to a square, and nothing of the file but the picture is kept: no place, no device.

password.title: Password
password.done: Password changed. Other browsers have to sign in again.
password.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.

oidc.title: Sign-in provider
oidc.only: This account signs in through the provider.
oidc.linked: Linked: you can sign in with the provider as well as with your password.
oidc.text: Link your account to the provider, then you can sign in with either. Your password confirms it is you.

sessions.title: Other browsers
sessions.text: Signs you out everywhere except here, for example after losing a phone.
sessions.done: Every other browser is signed out.

me.linked: Your account is linked to the provider.
me.setupFirst: The operator requires a second factor. Set it up here, then you can go on.

twofactor.title: Second factor
twofactor.lead: Besides the password, a code from an app on your phone (any authenticator app that takes a QR code). Recovery codes on paper get you in when the phone is gone.
twofactor.provider: You sign in through the provider; its second factor applies.
twofactor.scan: Scan this code with the app, or type the key below into it. Then give the code the app shows, and your password.
twofactor.qr: QR code for the authenticator app
twofactor.codeHint: Six digits. Or one of your recovery codes.
twofactor.passwordHint: Proves it is you at the keyboard.
twofactor.codesLead: Each one signs you in once, when the phone is not at hand. They are shown only now: copy them or save them as a file, and keep them apart from the phone.
twofactor.renewText: The old recovery codes stop working. Give your password to make new ones.
twofactor.disableText: From then on the password alone signs you in. Give it to turn the second factor off.
twofactor.lowCodes: Few recovery codes left. Make new ones while you can still sign in.
twofactor.loginText: The code from your app, or a recovery code.
twofactor.requiredText: The operator requires a second factor for every account that signs in with a password. Set it up to go on.

invite.noMail: Without a mail server nexbrand sends nothing: copy the link and pass it on yourself.
invite.once: The link works once. It is shown only now.

apiTokens.title: API tokens
apiTokens.text: For programs and AI tools in an editor (MCP). A token reads what you may read, limited to its clients: versions, the CI as code, the checks. A token of the level “drafts” also makes drafts; it can never publish.
apiTokens.name: Name, so you know it again
apiTokens.shownOnce: Token “{{name}}” made. It is shown only now. Copy it into your program; nexbrand keeps only a checksum.
apiTokens.header: As a header in nexdeck or n8n (HTTP Request, Header Auth)
apiTokens.off: The operator has not switched API tokens on. Ask them if you want to connect nexbrand with n8n or nexdeck.
apiTokens.offOperator: Switch them on under Settings → Server → API.
apiTokens.whatItDoesText: Every request carries the token in the header Authorization: Bearer, the answers are JSON. MCP speaks at /api/mcp. All the rest is in docs/api.md.
apiTokens.allSpaces: Every client I may see, later ones too

levels.readHint: Clients, versions, the CI as code, the checks. For build scripts and AI tools that build in the CI.
levels.draftHint: Also proposes versions as drafts, e.g. a redesign from the code. Publishing stays with people in nexbrand.

teams.text: Who works together. A team gets access to clients: when a client gives a team a right, every member has it.
teams.name: Name
teams.leadHint: As the lead you change the members. The operator changes name and colour.
teams.nobodyElse: Only people with an account can join a team, and so far there is only you. Invite someone first.
teams.rightsText: A team with a right gives it to all its members. Whoever has a higher right of their own keeps it.

suite.managed: This is kept in nexsuite now.
suite.managedAccounts: Accounts come from nexsuite. New people, blocking and roles there.
suite.managedSignIn: People sign in through nexsuite. Whether nexsuite checks itself or asks authentik is set there. Your own password stays as the emergency way in.
suite.managedMail: The mail server comes from nexsuite. With none set up there, nexbrand sends no mail. Your own setting is kept in case you disconnect.
suite.managedTeams: Teams come from nexsuite and apply in every connected app.
suite.managedProfile: Profile picture, name and address come from nexsuite and hold in every connected app. They are changed there.
suite.aloneText: nexbrand runs on its own, with its own accounts, teams, clients and settings. Connected to nexsuite, people, teams and clients come from there.
suite.connectedText: Connected to {{url}}. People, teams, clients and their access, sign-in and mail come from there.
suite.point1: Accounts, teams and clients are kept and matched.
suite.point2: Sign-in and mail are then set only in nexsuite.
suite.point3: You can disconnect at any time. nexbrand then keeps a copy and runs on its own again.
suite.codesNone: none yet, make them in nexsuite under Apps
suite.leave1: nexbrand keeps accounts, teams and clients with their CI and runs on its own.
suite.leave2: Whoever has no password of their own needs one from you afterwards.
suite.leave3: nexsuite forgets the app. You can connect again later.
suite.leaveCode: For when nexsuite cannot be reached. nexsuite learns of it once it runs again.
suite.withoutPassword: Without a password of their own: {{names}}. Give them one under Server, Accounts.
suite.emergencyText: For when nexsuite cannot be reached.
suite.emergencyHow: Whoever is signed in keeps working. You sign in at /notzugang with your own password; nexsuite sees it in its log. With an emergency code from nexsuite you disconnect nexbrand in an emergency.
suite.step1Text: You get the code in nexsuite under Apps, Connect. It is valid for 15 minutes.
suite.step2Text: Every account here belongs to a person in nexsuite from now on. Suggested by mail address and name. Clients, rights and history stay with it.
suite.step3Text: Clients from here go to nexsuite. If it already has the same one, you join them: the access from here comes along, and where someone already has a right there, the higher one counts. The CI stays in nexbrand.
suite.done1: From now on people sign in through nexsuite.
suite.done2: Accounts, teams and rights come from there and stay in step.
suite.done3: Your own password stays as the emergency way in at /notzugang.
suite.loginText: This nexbrand hangs on nexsuite. Sign in there.
suite.emergencyLoginText: Only for the operator, when nexsuite cannot be reached. The sign-in shows in nexsuite's log.
suite.managedSpace: nexsuite decides who sees this client. Change it there.
suite.managedTwoFactor: The second factor is set up in nexsuite (or in authentik when nexsuite signs in through it) and holds for every connected app.
suite.emergencyAccount: This is the emergency account of nexbrand. Password and second factor here are only for the emergency access when nexsuite cannot be reached (sign in at /notzugang). Otherwise you sign in through nexsuite like everybody.
suite.disconnectInSuite: You disconnect in nexsuite under Apps, or here with the emergency account of this app.
suite.teamsText: Teams the same way: if nexsuite has the matching team already, you join the two and the members from here come along. Otherwise it is made there.
suite.stillBlocked: Blocked from the time with nexsuite: {{names}}. Unblock them under Server, Accounts if they are to get in again.
suite.newPersonHint: “Make it in nexsuite”: nexsuite sends the person a link to set a password by mail; otherwise it is in nexsuite under People.
suite.freshMailed: New in nexsuite and asked by mail to set a password: {{names}}.
suite.freshInSuite: New in nexsuite but without a mail (no address or no mail server): {{names}}. Get the link to set the password in nexsuite under People, Edit.

clients.title: Clients
clients.text: Every client has its CI in versions; projects build on one of them.
clients.binText: Clients stay in the bin for 30 days, then they go with all their versions.
clients.purgeAsk: Delete {{name}} for good? This cannot be undone.
clients.fromSuite: Clients come from nexsuite: made there, they show up here and get their CI.

client.missing: This client does not exist, or you may not see it.
client.noneThen: There was no published version back then.
client.draftHolds: It holds once published; until then {{label}} holds.
client.draftOnly: There is no published version yet; projects build on this draft meanwhile.
client.olderUntil: You see version {{label}}, valid from {{from}} to {{until}}. The current one is {{current}}.
client.inReview: This draft is before the client for a review.
client.trashText: {{name}} goes into the bin with all versions and projects. It stays there for 30 days.
client.deleteDraftText: Delete the draft {{label}}? Published versions stay.
client.leaveText: There are unsaved changes. Close anyway?
client.name: Name
client.newVersionText: A new version starts as a draft, usually a copy of an existing one. The old one stays as it was.
client.publishText: Once published, the version never changes again. Projects on older versions stay where they are until somebody lifts them.
client.validFromHint: For an old CI you record afterwards, take the date it held from.
client.keptInSuite: Name, sector, contact, colour and who sees the client come from nexsuite and are changed there. The note is nexbrand's.
client.noCiText: The client is there, a CI it does not have yet. Start with the wizard, collect it from their website or style guide, or begin empty.
client.noCiSuite: The client comes from nexsuite. Its CI is made here: with the wizard, from their website or style guide, or empty.
client.noCiWizardText: Colours, fonts and logo step by step, with proposals and a review if you like.
client.noCiCollectText: From a website, a GitHub repository or a PDF style guide.
client.noCiEmptyText: An empty draft you fill in the editor.
client.noCiRead: Everyone with the right to write can make a CI.

projects.text: A project builds on a version and stays there until somebody lifts it. Its own colours hold in the project only.
projects.name: Project name
projects.missing: This project does not exist any more.
projects.pageText: Builds on version {{label}}. Its own colours hold here only; everything else comes from the version.
projects.behind: This project is on {{label}}, the current version is {{current}}. That is on purpose until somebody lifts it: a reprint looks like the first print.
projects.onDraftText: Builds on the draft {{label}}: the project sees changes to it at once.
projects.ownText: A colour with the name of one of the version replaces it ({{names}}); others come on top.

set.pangram: Freshly made, clearly said, well designed.

checks.none: Nothing found: every pair, logo and size passes.

ground_large_only.title: On {{a}}, large text only
ground_large_only.text: No colour of the palette reaches 4.5:1. Body text on {{a}} lacks a text colour.

ground_unreadable.title: Nothing reads on {{a}}
ground_unreadable.text: No colour of the palette reaches even 3:1 on {{a}}. Not a ground for text.

primary_as_text.title: {{a}} as text on {{b}}: {{ratio}}
primary_as_text.text: Links and small labels in {{a}} are too pale on {{b}}. From 24 px, or bold from 18.7 px, it is enough.

nearly_same.title: {{a}} and {{b}} are nearly the same
nearly_same.text: Colour distance ΔE {{delta}}. Below 5 hardly anybody sees a difference; one of them is probably redundant or a slip.

vision_deutan.title: {{a}} and {{b}} with green blindness
vision_deutan.text: Only ΔE {{delta}} apart. Never tell things apart by these two colours alone; add a sign or a word.

vision_protan.title: {{a}} and {{b}} with red blindness
vision_protan.text: Only ΔE {{delta}} apart. Never tell things apart by these two colours alone; add a sign or a word.

logo_mark.title: Logo “{{logo}}”: mark only {{ratio}}
logo_mark.text: Graphic parts need 3:1 to their ground (WCAG 1.4.11).

logo_word.title: Logo “{{logo}}”: lettering only {{ratio}}
logo_word.text: Graphic parts need 3:1 to their ground (WCAG 1.4.11).

body_small.title: Body text {{size}} px
body_small.text: Below 16 px, body text tires on a screen.

font_internal.title: {{font}}: in-house only
font_internal.text: Public pages and programs see it by name only; the file stays here.

font_system.title: {{font}} is a system font
font_system.text: Some devices lack it. Set a fallback.

checks.matrixText: The row is the text, the column the ground. Click a cell for a sample.
checks.matrixEmpty: A table needs at least two colours.
checks.sampleText: {{text}} on {{ground}}. This is how body text reads in this pair, on a phone in the sun too.

vision.title: How others see the palette
vision.normalHint: The palette as it is meant.
vision.deutanHint: Deuteranopia, the most common form; about one man in sixteen has a green weakness.
vision.protanHint: Protanopia: red looks dark and brownish.
vision.achromatHint: No colour, only lightness; black and white print too.
vision.clash: {{pairs}}: hard to tell apart. Never tell things apart by colour alone.

diff.nothing: No differences in colours, fonts and logos.

export.title: {{name}} as code
export.note: With steps 50 to 950 for every colour with a job. The JSON follows the W3C design tokens format; Figma, Style Dictionary and Tokens Studio read it.

shares.text: A link for a printer, a photographer or the client: read only, no account. Fonts kept in-house show by name only, the checks never.
shares.off: The operator has not allowed public pages (Settings, Server, Public pages).
shares.needPublished: Only a published version can be shared.
shares.passwordHint: Whoever has the link needs the password as well.
shares.internalHidden: Fonts kept in-house show by name only, never as a file.

reviews.none: No review yet. A draft goes to the client with “Put before the client”.
reviews.withdrawAsk: Withdraw the review? The link stops working.
reviews.chosen: {{who}} chose “{{label}}”; it became the published version.
reviews.newText: The client sees each direction on a sample page, comments and chooses one. The choice is published without anybody here clicking again.
reviews.label: Name once chosen
reviews.labelHint: The version's name once the client chose.
reviews.sender: Sender, as the client sees it
reviews.message: A few words to the client
reviews.messageHint: e.g. Here are two directions for your new look.
reviews.onlyOne: Other drafts of this client can go along as alternatives.

preview.label: Sample page in this CI
preview.name: Your name
preview.headline: {{name}}: well made, close by.
preview.text: This is how body text reads in this CI. Long enough to tell whether the font carries and the colour holds on its ground.

editor.name: Name
editor.note: Note, e.g. what the colour is for
editor.noColors: No colours yet. Add one, or start with the workbench.
editor.neutrals: Neutrals with a touch of the main colour
editor.fitsText: Computed from the main colour. A click takes the colour in.

harmony.complementText: Opposite on the colour wheel. The greatest distance, for a single accent.
harmony.neighboursText: Left and right of it. Calm, belonging together.
harmony.triadText: Three evenly spaced hues. Lively, needs plenty of neutrals.
harmony.splitText: Two hues beside the complement. Contrast, but softer.

editor.scaleNote: The steps go into the export (e.g. --color-main-600) without an entry of their own. A click takes a step in as a colour of its own.
editor.fontLicenseNote: “In-house only” keeps the file in the house: public pages and programs see the name only. System fonts are recorded by name only.
editor.logoNote: Logos are drawn in Figma or Illustrator and uploaded here. Until then word marks from the name, font and main colour stand in.

gen.whiteOk: {{name}} carries white text ({{ratio}}), good for buttons.
gen.whiteBad: No white text on {{name}} ({{ratio}}). Use dark text.
gen.clear: Keep at least the height of the capital letter free around the logo.
gen.distort: Do not stretch, turn or recolour the logo.

pairs.fraunces-inter: A soft serif with character over a neutral text face: crafted without looking old-fashioned.
pairs.playfair-dmsans: Strong contrast in the headings, plain body text: fine, and still easy to read.
pairs.spacegrotesk-inter: Technical and clear, good for software and anything that wants to move ahead.
pairs.outfit-sourceserif: Geometric headings, a serif in the text: modern and pleasant for long reads.
pairs.nunito-nunito: Round shapes, friendly; one family for everything, the weights tell apart.
pairs.lora-dmsans: A calm book serif with a clear sans: trustworthy, e.g. for a practice or a law firm.

wizard.title: New client
wizard.text: For a client without a CI: design it in the workbench, checked while you build, agreed with the client. For a client with a CI: start empty and record it.
wizard.brief: How should the brand feel? (for the suggestions, may stay empty)
wizard.briefHint: A few words are enough: trade, mood, audience.
wizard.startText: Four ways to a first palette. Everything after can be changed.
wizard.proposeNote: The directions come from the keywords of the description. Then nexbrand checks the numbers and darkens the main colour until a button with white text and a link on a light ground reach 4.5:1.

a.label: Direction A, close to the description
a.why: The hue sits where “{{mood}}” is at home; a neighbouring hue as accent, neutrals with a touch of the main colour.

b.label: Direction B, with a counterpoint
b.why: The same hue, stronger, with the complement as accent; takes “{{second}}” along as well.

c.label: Direction C, reserved
c.why: Little colour, much calm. The brand lives on type and space here, not on signal colours.

wizard.pictureText: A mood picture, a photo of the shop, an old poster. nexbrand counts the colours in it and suggests roles; the picture stays in your browser.
wizard.colorText: A colour the client brings. Fitting neutrals come along; the next step suggests accents.
wizard.emptyText: For a client that has a CI already: start empty and record colours, fonts and logos from the style guide.
wizard.colorsText: Name, role, value. Every change runs the checks on the right again.
wizard.fontsText: Pairs that work together, all under free licences and shipped with nexbrand.
wizard.bodySample: Body text in {{font}}: easy to read, in long paragraphs too.
wizard.fontsLater: Fonts of your own, with files and licence notes, come after creating, under Edit.
wizard.sizesText: A base size and a ratio; every step follows from them.
wizard.logoText: The logo is drawn in Figma or Illustrator. Until it is there, word marks from the name, heading font and main colour stand in, so developers can start building.
wizard.logoUploaded: Uploaded; the word marks stay as stand-ins.
wizard.noLogoYet: No logo yet: the word mark stands in.
wizard.finishText: The client starts with the draft 1.0. With a review the client sees the directions on a sample page, comments and chooses one; the choice is published.
wizard.workedWhy: The version from the workbench. Always included.
wizard.stillHints_one: The checks still have {{count}} hint. Creating works anyway; the client does not see it.
wizard.stillHints_other: The checks still have {{count}} hints. Creating works anyway; the client does not see them.
wizard.noReview: A review needs the right to manage the client, and public pages the operator has allowed.
wizard.withReview: Create and put before the client
wizard.asideEmpty: Once there are colours, a sample page in the CI shows here, with the checks running again on every change.
wizard.aiHint: Your AI proposes a hue, a pair of fonts and a reason; nexbrand then works out the colours itself.
wizard.rulesHint: Without AI, the directions come from key words in the description.
wizard.aiFailed: The AI did not answer ({{reason}}). The directions come from the key words.
wizard.notAllowed: Only the operator makes clients here. They can allow members under Settings.
wizard.fromSuite: Clients come from nexsuite. Make the client there; here it then gets its CI.
wizard.hasCi: This client has a CI already. What you build here becomes a new version as a draft.

contrast.title: Contrast checker
contrast.text: Two colours, every check at once. Suggests the nearest colour of the same hue that passes.
contrast.body: Body text at 16 px. Is it comfortable to read, on a phone in the sun too?
contrast.small: Small print at 12 px, e.g. for footnotes and prices.
contrast.better: Nearest text colour with 4.5:1 on this ground: {{hex}} ({{ratio}}), same hue {{hue}}°.

review.title: Your new look, {{name}}
review.textMany: Here are {{count}} directions, each shown on a sample page. Say what you like and what you don't. When one fits, choose it; it becomes your binding CI.
review.textOne: Here is the draft, shown on a sample page. Say what you like and what you don't. When it fits, choose it; it becomes your binding CI.
review.thanks: Thank you! You chose “{{label}}”. This is your CI now; the agency works on with it.
review.chooseText: It becomes your CI. Later changes the agency makes as a new version; this one stays on record.

ai.title: AI
ai.text: Your own AI service sorts the colours and fonts found when collecting and proposes three directions for a new client in the wizard. You pay for its key yourself. The AI never invents a colour value: nexbrand measures them and checks the contrast again.
ai.off: The operator has not switched on AI.
ai.offOperator: Switch it on under Settings, Server, Collecting and AI.
ai.tiles: Fill in the address of a service
ai.address: Address (any service that speaks the usual chat interface)
ai.keyNone: none (a service at home may need none)
ai.modelsFound_one: {{count}} model found: address and key are right.
ai.modelsFound_other: {{count}} models found: address and key are right.
ai.switchHint: Collecting then offers “Sort with AI”, the wizard “Propose with AI”.
ai.switchIncomplete: Save an address and a model first.
ai.whereItGoes: What was collected (colour values, names, where they were found) or your description goes to the address above, nothing else. What happens to it there is up to that service and its conditions.
ai.eventsText: Every request to your service, word for word, 14 days long. Shown as text, never as a page.

collect.title: Collect
collect.text: Colours, fonts and logos from websites, GitHub repositories and PDF style guides. The values are measured; rules or your AI only sort them. They become a draft, or you check a site against the CI.
collect.noCurrent: This client has no published version yet to check against.
collect.useAiHint: Your AI gives roles and names and leaves out what does not belong. It sees only the measured values.
collect.aiNotReady: Without AI, fixed rules sort: the most frequent colourful one leads, greys become neutrals.
collect.privacy: The server fetches websites and repositories, never an address in the own network. A PDF is added to the client's files.
collect.nothing: Nothing found. The page may load its colours with JavaScript only; a repository or a style guide helps then.
collect.sortedByAi: Sorted by your AI. What is ticked is taken; role and name can be changed.
collect.sortedByRules: Sorted by rules. Nearly identical colours and tiny shares are unticked.
collect.name: Name
collect.logosText: Pictures found with “logo” in their name, icons and preview images. Taking one adds it to the client's files.
collect.takeHint_one: {{count}} colour becomes a new draft. Fonts replace those of the current version, logos are added, everything else stays. Publishing happens on the client's page.
collect.takeHint_other: {{count}} colours become a new draft. Fonts replace those of the current version, logos are added, everything else stays. Publishing happens on the client's page.
collect.takeNewHint_one: A new client with {{count}} colour as a draft.
collect.takeNewHint_other: A new client with {{count}} colours as a draft.
collect.label: Collected on {{date}}
collect.auditText: Every colour found next to the nearest one of the CI (ΔE 2000). Nearly right usually means a wrong shade in a style sheet.
collect.near: Nearly right, ΔE {{de}}. The CI colour is probably meant.
collect.foreign: Not in the CI ({{share}} % of what was found).

problems.not_public: is in the own network and is never fetched.
problems.bad_address: is not a valid web address.
problems.not_a_repo: is not the address of a GitHub repository.
